title: Server JS
body:
[[Node.js]]

JavaScript running on the server rather than in the browser, which in this course means
[[Node.js]]. The lecture headings use this name; [[Node JS]] and Node are the same thing.

What changes when the same language moves to the other side of the wire: there is no [[DOM]],
no `window`, and no [[Web APIs|browser Web APIs]], because there is no page. In their place are
the filesystem (`fs`), the network (`http`), paths (`path`), and process information, none of
which a browser would ever let a script touch. The language is identical; the host is not.

See [[Server Side]] for what belongs on this side and why.
